speaker: Benvolio Montague
text: Okay, I think we're all here. Hi, Juliet. Thanks for making the time.

speaker: Juliet Capulet
text: Hi, Benvolio. Hi, Romeo. Thanks for coming over.

speaker: Benvolio Montague
text: So, quick intros for the notes. I'm product on the Montague side, Romeo's the staff engineer who'll actually build most of our half.

speaker: Juliet Capulet
text: And I'm head of product at Capulet, I own the spec on our side. Tybalt, our engineering lead, sent me with a question, so, fair warning.

speaker: Benvolio Montague
text: Noted. Do you want to walk us through scope?

speaker: Juliet Capulet
text: Yeah. So, short version. Balcony App does field inspections in warehouses. Inspectors walk a site, take photos, log findings, sign the report. Right now that data stops at Balcony. Schema Bridge is a shared format for an inspection record plus a bridge that moves those records into Mesh Routing, so your side can route work off them.

speaker: Romeo Montague
text: And the record is the five fields in your draft? I skimmed it this morning.

speaker: Juliet Capulet
text: Right. Site, inspector, photos, findings, signed at. I wrote it this morning, so it's rough.

speaker: Romeo Montague
text: No, it's a good start. The part I'd push on is the sync. You've got a nightly batch.

speaker: Juliet Capulet
text: I do. It felt simple.

speaker: Romeo Montague
text: It is simple. But if an inspector signs something at nine in the morning, nobody downstream sees it until the next day. I'd rather we send events. Each signed inspection goes over as its own event, when it's signed. And if one fails it doesn't take the whole night with it.

speaker: Juliet Capulet
text: Huh. Okay. I like that. I'm not attached to the batch, I just didn't want to overbuild.

speaker: Benvolio Montague
text: Can I jump in on timing? Ducal Freight is the pilot, and I'd love to show them something real soon. What if we aim for a demo this Friday?

speaker: Juliet Capulet
text: This Friday. Okay. That's, um, ambitious.

speaker: Juliet Capulet
text: We've got our own release go or no-go Friday morning, but a demo in the afternoon could work. Let's do it.

speaker: Benvolio Montague
text: Great. I'll set it up with Ducal.

speaker: Juliet Capulet
text: Okay, so, Tybalt's question. His worry is, if Balcony depends on Mesh Routing, and Mesh Routing goes down, do our inspectors stop working? They can't wait on someone else's service.

speaker: Romeo Montague
text: Totally fair question. And honestly, he should worry about that, I would.

speaker: Juliet Capulet
text: So what's the answer?

speaker: Romeo Montague
text: A local queue. Balcony doesn't talk to Mesh Routing directly when an inspector signs something. It drops the event into a queue on the device. When Mesh Routing is reachable, the queue drains. When it's not, events just wait. The inspector never knows the difference.

speaker: Juliet Capulet
text: So Balcony keeps working no matter what's happening on your side.

speaker: Romeo Montague
text: That's the idea. Our outage becomes a delay, not a failure.

speaker: Juliet Capulet
text: I think Tybalt can live with that. He'll want to see it, though.

speaker: Romeo Montague
text: I'll prototype it. Give me a couple of days.

speaker: Benvolio Montague
text: What about the other open question in the doc? Field versioning?

speaker: Juliet Capulet
text: Right. If we add a field to the inspection record, or change one, who decides? Is it us, is it you, is it both?

speaker: Romeo Montague
text: Hmm. I don't think we should answer that in the first meeting.

speaker: Benvolio Montague
text: Agreed, let's leave it open. But let's not leave it open forever.

speaker: Juliet Capulet
text: Fair. I'll keep it in the spec as an open question.

speaker: Benvolio Montague
text: Okay, action items, so we don't lose them. Juliet?

speaker: Juliet Capulet
text: I'll do a spec v2 by Wednesday. Switch the sync to events, add the local queue, and keep versioning as an open question.

speaker: Romeo Montague
text: And I'll prototype the queue.

speaker: Benvolio Montague
text: And I'll set up Friday with Ducal. Anything else?

speaker: Juliet Capulet
text: No, I think that's good. Thanks, both of you. This was easier than I expected.

speaker: Romeo Montague
text: Don't tell Tybalt that, he'll get suspicious.

speaker: Juliet Capulet
text: Ha. I'll tell him you answered his question. Talk soon.
